title: Ankle injury and Ottawa rules
stem: Cubicle 16. Ms Leung, 34, went over on her left ankle stepping off a kerb 2 hours ago. She limped in. Examine her ankle and foot, decide whether she needs an X-ray, and explain the management.

phases.title: Examine
phases.goal: The ankle, the foot, and above and below.

phases.title: Explain
phases.goal: The fracture, the boot, and warning signs.

notes:
Checked against the Ottawa ankle and foot rules (Stiell 1992–1994), BOAST 'Management of ankle fractures' (2016) and NICE CKS (sprains).

Ottawa ankle rule: X-ray if pain in the malleolar zone and any of: bone tenderness along the posterior edge or tip of the lateral malleolus (distal 6 cm), or of the medial malleolus, or inability to bear weight (4 steps) immediately and in the ED. Foot rule: pain in the midfoot and tenderness at the base of the 5th metatarsal or the navicular, or inability to bear weight. Sensitivity near 100%; applies to adults (and children over 5 with care).

Also examine the proximal fibula (Maisonneuve), the Achilles tendon (Simmonds/Thompson test), and neurovascular status. Weber classification by the fibular fracture level relative to the syndesmosis: A below (usually stable), B at the level (stability depends on the medial side — medial tenderness, medial clear space widening), C above (unstable). A stable Weber B can be treated in a boot and weight-bearing as tolerated (BOAST/CROSSBAT), while talar shift needs orthopaedic fixation.

Your notes list 'Ankle and Ottawa rules' without detail.

steps.label: Examine
steps.hint: Look, feel the Ottawa points, proximal fibula, Achilles, move, weight-bearing, neurovascular.

Look.r: Swelling and bruising over the lateral malleolus. No deformity.

Ottawa points.t: Posterior edge and tip of the lateral malleolus (distal 6 cm)
Ottawa points.mark: Palpates the lateral malleolus posterior edge

Ottawa points.t: Posterior edge and tip of the medial malleolus
Base of the 5th metatarsal and the navicular

Ottawa points.r: Only with a lot of help.

X-ray.r: Oblique fracture of the distal fibula at the level of the syndesmosis (Weber B). Medial clear space normal, talus not shifted.
X-ray.mark: Identifies a Weber B fracture and checks talar shift

steps.label: Explain
steps.hint: Stable Weber B: boot, weight-bear as tolerated, fracture clinic; safety-net.

opts.t: A break of the outer ankle bone, but the joint is lined up and stable. A walking boot, weight-bear as comfortable, pain relief, fracture clinic in a week, and a repeat X-ray.
opts.tz: 你外踝嗰條骨斷咗，不過關節對得好正，亦都穩定。會俾你著一隻行路靴，唔痛就可以落地行，食止痛藥。一個禮拜後去骨科門診，再照 X 光。
opts.mark: Explains a stable Weber B and its management

opts.t: Elevate, move the toes, come back for severe pain, numbness or calf swelling (clot risk)
opts.tz: 隻腳要墊高，郁吓啲腳趾。如果好痛、麻痺，或者小腿腫，就要即刻返嚟，因為有機會係血栓。

opts.t: Non-weight-bearing in a full plaster for 6 weeks
opts.tz: 要打全腳石膏，六個禮拜唔可以落地。
opts.r: A stable Weber B does well in a boot with early weight-bearing.
